questions.question_text: Figure 1.47 shows the inflows and outflows on the Nile water and rainfall graphs for the source areas. State the amount of water that initially comes from the White Nile.

marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for stating 75 billion cumecs / m³.

questions.question_text: State the amount of water that joins the Blue Nile.

marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for stating 24 billion cumecs / m³.

questions.question_text: Describe the rainfall pattern for the source of the Blue Nile.

points: The rainfall pattern for the Blue Nile is very seasonal / monsoonal [1]
Peak flow / heavy rainfall in summer (June to September) [1]
Low flow / dry period in winter (October to February / March) [1]
Data quantification: e.g. over 250 mm of rainfall in July, about 800 mm between June and September, or less than 50 mm/month between October and February [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks: 1 mark for seasonal/monsoonal nature, 1 mark for peak in summer/low in winter, 1 mark for quantification with figures.

questions.question_text: Figure 1.48 shows the changes in the flow of water in the Nile before and after the building of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), completed in 2020. State the maximum flow in the Nile without the GERD.

marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for stating approximately 7750 m³/s (acceptable range 7600–7800 m³/s).

questions.question_text: State the maximum flow in the Nile with the GERD.
Compare the flow of the Blue Nile without the GERD and with the GERD.

points: The flow of the Blue Nile without the GERD was very seasonal [1]
Peak flow in August / autumn without the GERD [1]
The flow of the Blue Nile after the GERD was built was the same year-round [1]
Award 1 mark for quantification (e.g. peak of ~7750 m³/s vs regulated flow) [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks: The flow of the Blue Nile without the GERD was very seasonal [1], with a peak flow in August/autumn [1], whereas the flow of the Blue Nile after the GERD was built was the same year-round [1]. Award 1 mark for quantification.
